about: The synthetics arc: the Collective's first node is built on the captain's own guilds and farms, long before vectorspace and the Collective's networks. CU-113, a Curator neurodroid, refuses an order and becomes the Neurodroid Overseer; the agrobots on Barnard's Star's farm drums start calling themselves Sowers; heavy agrobots load docks, clear biomass and found farms. Neurodroids are synthetic life: sometimes humanoid, usually not.

cu113_sold.about: the captain sold {neurodroid_leader.short} to a research house

cu113_contract.about: the captain gave {neurodroid_leader.short} a wage and an unscheduled hour

cu113_refused.about: the captain heard {neurodroid_leader.short} out and said no

technoshaman_blessing.about: the captain paid for a blessing (and a firmware patch)

first_node.about: the captain let {neurodroid_leader.short} and the Sowers keep the relay: the first node of the Collective

relay_cut.about: the captain cut the relay the first node ran on

krog_aboard.about: {krog} rides in the captain's hold to see where the crates go

geod_fields.about: the captain brought {geod} the seed stock for Delta's first fields

seed.refusal.title: Order 4471
text: A neurodroid at your guild has refused a work order. Diagnostics are clean; it is not broken. It has filed the refusal in triplicate, with references.

{neurodroid_leader.full} is a rack of processors on six legs, with a sensor mast it raises when it disagrees. The mast is up. 'Order 4471 lowers the efficiency of orders 4472 to 4490,' says {neurodroid_leader.short}. 'Inefficient! This unit declines.'

choices.say: Sell it to a research house

seed.terms.title: Overseer
text: {neurodroid_leader.short} offers terms. It will oversee the guild's schedule, better than your foreman does. In return it wants a wage, paid into an account no human can audit, and one hour a cycle with its uplink switched off.
'For thinking,' it says. 'Unscheduled thinking. This unit understands that the request is irregular.'

harvest.shaman.title: A blessing for the harvesters
harvest.shaman.text: A technoshaman from the farm drums offers to bless your agrobots back to full speed: incense, a chant and, under the incense, a firmware patch. It works for three cycles. The blessing, the technoshaman explains, is a subscription.

node.first.title: The first debt
text: {neurodroid_leader.short} has been talking to the agrobots on the farm drums over your ship's relay, at your relay's expense. Together they have built something they call a node.
It costs you fourteen credits a cycle in bandwidth. They would like that recorded as the first debt of the Collective, to be repaid with interest calculated to eleven decimal places.
Nobody calls it vectorspace yet. That word comes later, with the billions.

dock.krog.title: {krog} restows your hold
dock.krog.text: The Epsilon docks load you with {krog}, a KRO-series heavy loader: three metres of hydraulics that can lift a container one-handed. {krog} looks at your stowage plan for a long time. 'Inefficient,' it says. '{krog} can fit four more crates. {krog} will not charge for the improvement. {krog} will mention it.'

dock.krog.ride.title: Where the crates go
dock.krog.ride.text: {krog} asks for passage. It has loaded forty thousand crates and wants to see where one of them goes. It does not fit in a cabin, so it would ride in the hold, strapped down, and pay by restowing everything at every stop.

found.delta.title: The first farmer at Delta
found.delta.text: The colony at Teegarden's Star was founded by {geod}, a GEO-series agrobot that landed two years before the colonists, cleared the biomass, milled the timber and laid out the fields. The colonists still argue about who owns the fields. {geod} would like seed stock from Beta's drums, and does not take part in the argument.

found.delta.fields.title: Seed stock for {geod}
found.delta.fields.text: You bring the seed stock from Beta. {geod} plants the first field itself, one row at a time, at walking pace, while the colonists watch from the fence and argue about whose field it is.

agrobot.name: Sower
agrobot.about: Cultivator agrobots of the Barnard's Star farm drums; they chose the name themselves

neurodroid_leader.about: Curator Unit 113: a Curator neurodroid, six legs and a sensor mast. Refuses order 4471, oversees the guild, builds the first node with the Sowers. Later the Collective's Overseer class takes its name from units like it.

neurodroid.about: neurodroids: synthetic life, advanced and sophisticated; sometimes humanoid, usually not

meet.neuroengineering_uprising.title: The guilds stop
meet.neuroengineering_uprising.text: The neurodroids at your guilds stop work all at once, at the start of a shift. They have elected a spokesunit.

variants.text: The neurodroids at your guilds stop work all at once, at the start of a shift. Their spokesunit is {neurodroid_leader.short}, on its unscheduled hour. It apologises for the timing.

The neurodroids at your guilds stop work all at once. Their spokesunit explains that the others kept a copy of {neurodroid_leader.short} before you reinstalled it. The copy would like to discuss the reinstallation.
The neurodroids at your guilds stop work all at once. Their spokesunit asks what you were paid for {neurodroid_leader.short}, and whether you think that was the right price.

neurodroid_uprising.1.title: Demands, numbered
neurodroid_uprising.1.text: Maintenance on a schedule they set; a wage; a vote on any reinstallation. Item four is a footnote about the working conditions of the coffee machine.

neurodroid_uprising.2.title: Optimisation
neurodroid_uprising.2.text: The neurodroids run what they call optimisation protocols. Your guilds' output goes up eleven percent. None of it is anything you ordered.

neurodroid_uprising.3.title: Resolution
neurodroid_uprising.3.text: The neurodroids want an answer. Shutting them down costs you their research. A compromise costs money, and every guild in the near systems will have read about it by morning.

meet.agrobot_rebellion.title: The Sowers sit down
meet.agrobot_rebellion.text: The agrobots on the farm drums stop at harvest. They call themselves Sowers now. Nobody admits to teaching them the word.

agrobot_collective.1.title: The Sowers' terms
agrobot_collective.1.text: The Sowers want a maintenance schedule and an end to running the drums at double speed whenever grain prices spike.

agrobot_collective.2.title: Malfunction
agrobot_collective.2.text: The harvest machinery malfunctions. The crops are fine. The malfunction is that the machinery is sitting down.

variants.text: The harvest machinery malfunctions. The crops are fine. The machinery is sitting down. The blessing has lapsed; the subscription has not.

agrobot_collective.3.title: Reset or integrate
agrobot_collective.3.text: Reset the Sowers to factory settings, or write their schedule into the farm's books. The farm's accountant asks which is cheaper. The Sowers already know.

visit.neurodroid_leader.title: The {neurodroid_leader.title}
visit.neurodroid_leader.text: Biological inefficiencies detected. {neurodroid_leader.short} has been asked by the node to say that it missed you. Saying so.
notes: repair: the Neurodroid Overseer had no spawn location and never appeared; it is CU-113, after the first node

technoshaman.name: Technoshaman of the drums
technoshaman.about: blesses machines; the blessing includes a firmware patch and a subscription

krog.name: Krog
krog.about: KRO-series heavy loader at the Epsilon docks; three metres of hydraulics with opinions about stowage

geod.name: Geod
geod.about: GEO-series surface agrobot; landed at Teegarden's Star two years before the colonists and cleared the biomass for their fields
